r0010: The European Court of Human Rights (Third Section), sitting as a Chamber composed of:
r0011:
Mr	G. Ress, President,
		L. Caflisch,
		P. Kūris,
		R. Türmen,
		J. Hedigan,
	Mrs	M. Tsatsa-Nikolovska,
		H.S. Greve, judges,
and Mr V. Berger, Section Registrar,
r0012: Having deliberated in private on 17 October 2002,
r0013: Delivers the following judgment, which was adopted on that date:
r0015: 1.  The case originated in an application (no. 42739/98) against the Republic of Turkey lodged with the European Commission of Human Rights (“the Commission”) under former Article 25 of the Convention for the Protection of Human Rights and Fundamental Freedoms (“the Convention”) by a Turkish national, Yaşar Özel (“the applicant”), on 1 July 1998.
r0016: 2.  The applicant, who had been granted legal aid, was represented before the Court by Mr Kırdök, a lawyer practising in Istanbul. The Turkish Government (“the Government”) were represented by their Agent.
r0017: 3.  The applicant alleged, in particular, that he had been the victim of a violation of Article 6 § 1 on account of the lack of independence and impartiality of the National Security Court (*cour de sûreté de l’Etat*) which had tried and convicted him, and of the unfairness of the proceedings before that court.
r0018: 4.  The application was transmitted to the Court on 1 November 1998, when Protocol No. 11 to the Convention came into force (Article 5 § 2 of Protocol No. 11).
r0019: 5.  The application was allocated to the First Section of the Court (Rule 52 § 1 of the Rules of Court).
